title: Ice maker water supply fault
shortDescription: No water detected at fill during ice cycle.
fullDescription: IM-01 on Sub-Zero built-in ice makers means the fill valve opened but no water reached the mold. Common causes include a closed saddle valve, clogged inlet screen, or frozen fill tube. Inspect water line and warm any frozen sections.

causes.cause: Closed or partially closed supply valve

fixSteps.title: Check water
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the water shutoff behind the unit is fully open.

fixSteps.title: Thaw fill tube
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off ice maker and warm fill tube with warm cloth.

whenToCallPro: If water line is intact but no fill.
videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero ice maker IM-01 no water

faq.a: Not recommended — use filtered plumbed supply.

title: Ice bin full sensor fault
shortDescription: Bin-full sensor not reporting correct state.
fullDescription:
Sub-Zero ice makers use an optical or lever sensor to detect a full bin. IM-02 means the signal is stuck. Ice production may halt even with an empty bin, or continue until jammed.

Clean the sensor area; remove any frost that blocks the optical beam.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove ice bin, wipe sensor windows dry.

videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero ice maker IM-02 bin sensor

faq.a: Unit stops when bin ~90 percent full.

title: Harvest motor fault
shortDescription: Ice harvest motor did not complete rotation in time.
fullDescription: IM-03 indicates the ice harvesting mechanism stalled. Typically this is caused by a jammed ice cube or a failing motor. Power off, clear any ice debris, then restart.

fixSteps.title: Clear jam
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove ice, clear mold area.

title: Evaporator temperature sensor fault
shortDescription: Sensor monitoring freezing plate reads out of range.
fullDescription: IM-04 means the thermistor that monitors the ice mold is reporting invalid values. Ice cycle timing becomes unreliable. Service call to replace.

title: Drain pump fault
shortDescription: Drain pump fails to evacuate meltwater.
fullDescription: Standalone Sub-Zero UC-15IO units have an internal drain pump to discharge meltwater. IM-05 indicates a pump fault — typically a clogged impeller or failed motor. Pump trap should be cleaned routinely.

fixSteps.title: Clean pump trap
fixSteps.instruction: Access drain pump, remove trap, clear debris.

title: Compressor fault
shortDescription: Refrigeration compressor not starting or over-current.
fullDescription: IM-06 indicates the ice maker's dedicated compressor did not start. Sealed system repair required.

faq.a: Sub-Zero sealed system has extended warranty — check your paperwork.

title: Service filter reminder
fullDescription: IM-07 illuminates when the installed water filter has dispensed the rated volume. Replace with a genuine Sub-Zero filter and reset the indicator.

fixSteps.title: Replace filter
fixSteps.instruction: Rotate old cartridge and install new.

title: Condenser cleaning reminder
fullDescription: IM-08 appears every 6 months to remind owners to vacuum the condenser coil grille. Dust on the coil reduces cooling and can eventually trigger high-temperature faults.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum grille
fixSteps.instruction: Remove lower grille and vacuum condenser.

title: Drain Pump Fault
shortDescription: Built-in drain pump did not run when commanded.
fullDescription: Sub-Zero ice maker IM-09 sets when the drain pump is commanded on but the controller does not see expected current draw or level change. Drain pump failures lead to sump overflow.

fixSteps.title: Read service log
fixSteps.instruction: Use the diagnostic menu to read the latest fault log entry and timestamp.

fixSteps.title: Inspect related hardware
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the component implicated by the code; clean or reseat connectors.

fixSteps.title: Replace OEM part
fixSteps.instruction: Order and install Sub-Zero OEM replacement; clear the code.

whenToCallPro: Sub-Zero recommends an authorized factory-certified technician for sealed-system repairs.

faq.a: Authorized service can pull diagnostic logs but on-site repair is generally required.
